# Hardcoding inventory (generated by tools/literal_scan.py)

> **First principle:** a value the business may change is configuration; a text a user reads is a text element; a value fixed by a standard or by SAP syntax is a named constant.

## Before / after

| | Before (f10b8f0) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Literals in production ABAP | 1 909 | 1440 |
| User-facing text (1) | 516 | 0 |
| Technical value (2) | 274 | 0 |
| Legitimate (3) | 1 119 | 1440 |

Same scanner and allow-list for both columns. Texts moved to message class ZCD_OPS (built only through `ZCL_CD_OPS_UTIL=>TEXT( )`) or to text symbols of the reports and of `ZCL_CD_HCK_REPORT_HTML` / `ZCL_CD_OPS_ALERT_POLICY`; values moved to named constants in the area types interfaces (`gc_check_code`, `gc_msg`, `gc_param`, `gc_param_default`, `gc_rule_keyword`, `gc_engine_key`, …), class constants, the generated `lif_c` interfaces of the configuration apps, or SAP constants (`cl_abap_typedescr=>typekind_*`). The check `no_inline_texts` in `tools/portable_checks.py` keeps it at zero.

## Now

Literals in production ABAP: **1440** — user-facing text (1): **0**, technical value (2): **0**, legitimate (3): **1440**.

Category 3 = declarations (CONSTANTS / TYPES / DATA / PARAMETERS / types interfaces), separators and format characters, names SAP syntax requires as literals (CALL FUNCTION, AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT / ID, MESSAGE TYPE), and allow-listed lines (`tools/literal_allowlist.txt`, each with its reason).

| File | Text (1) | Value (2) | Legitimate (3) |
|---|---|---|---|

Files not listed have no category 1 or 2 literal.
